discovery-9f193cf71a3b301fd8abed978abd6b.title: Marching to Independence: Lancaster Soldiers at the Battle of Fort Lee
discovery-9f193cf71a3b301fd8abed978abd6b.description: How did ordinary men from Lancaster County end up on the front lines of the American Revolution? Step back in time with living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the harrowing story of Clotz's Battalion-- part of the legendary "Flying Camp" mobile reserve. Relive the tension of November 1776 at the Battle of Fort Lee, discover the courageous stories of local soldiers fighting for a brand-new nation, and see how modern historians uncover the past to keep their legacy alive. Don't miss this immersive journey into the fight for independence! Registration is encouraged! A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Presenter Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.
discovery-9f193cf71a3b301fd8abed978abd6b.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-b2835165e32dc51095b0f0ff100c17.title: Well Rooted: Genealogy Drop In
discovery-b2835165e32dc51095b0f0ff100c17.description: Are you hitting a "brick wall" in your family tree research? Whether you are a seasoned researcher or just starting to wonder about your heritage, the library is here to help! Join us on the 3rd Thursday of every month at 3:00 PM for our Genealogy Drop-In Program. Our volunteers will be on hand to help you navigate databases, interpret census records, and organize your findings. If you have a specific research goal or a particularly tricky question, we encourage you to reach out to us ahead of time. Providing details in advance allows us to prepare resources specifically for your search. Send us an email at info@mtpl.info When: 3rd Thursdays at 3:00 PM Where: Morgan Center B Cost: Free and open to the public
discovery-b2835165e32dc51095b0f0ff100c17.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-8dd60812f1994e3fea700517275550.description: Make Lancaster Public Library a stop on your First Friday culture crawl! Downtown Lancaster springs to life on the First Friday of each month. Art galleries, studios, museums, restaurants, shops, and attractions in downtown Lancaster stay open late while people head out to enjoy the festive atmosphere, dining, art, and entertainment. discovery-619d3222bf214b5a8e5d5ca6e03857.title: Coffee & Crossing: Washington's Winter of 1776
discovery-619d3222bf214b5a8e5d5ca6e03857.description: Grab a piping-hot mug of authentic colonial coffee and step right into the high-stakes winter of 1776! Join living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the bold strategy, hidden Lancaster County connections, and dramatic reality behind Washington’s famous crossing of the Delaware and the epic 1st Battle of Trenton. Separate fact from fiction, sip historical brews, and discover how coffee and courage helped turn the tide of the Revolutionary War! Registration is encouraged A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.
discovery-619d3222bf214b5a8e5d5ca6e03857.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-4476b5efc9b264ee6859e3e464cf85.title: Victorian Christmas: Customs & Costumes
discovery-4476b5efc9b264ee6859e3e464cf85.description: Step back in time and discover how many of our favorite holiday traditions began! Join historian Lynnette Miller from Landis Valley for a fascinating look into the holiday customs, festive decorations, and seasonal fashions of the Victorian era. From decorated evergreen trees and handmade gifts to period-appropriate winter attire, this presentation explores how Victorian-era families celebrated the holiday season. The presentation will be followed by a Q&A session with the audience. Free and open to the public. Registration is requested.
discovery-4476b5efc9b264ee6859e3e464cf85.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-0b74cae0507258597a6fead09bb9c1.title: The Neverland Book Club
discovery-0b74cae0507258597a6fead09bb9c1.description: The book club where our reading tastes never grow up! Every month, we'll discuss one middle-grade or young adult book. Here are just a few of the reasons to join: - Short books (easier to read before book club!) - Revisiting nostalgic stories or finding new favorites - Discussing meaningful topics and themes (you might be surprised by how deep children's literature can get!) Registration is encouraged, but walk-ins are welcome! Reading List: January 7: Bridge to Terabithia by Katherine Paterson February 4: Roll of Thunder, Hear My Cry by Mildred D. Taylor March 4: Redwall by Brian Jacques April 1: Speak by Laurie Halse Anderson May 6: The Outsiders by S. E. Hinton June 3: Matilda by Roald Dahl July 1: Holes by Louis Sachar August 5: Looking for Alaska by John Green September 2: A Wrinkle in Time by Madeleine L'Engle October 7: The Giver by Lois Lowry November 4: The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett December 2: Charlotte's Web by E. B. White This is a book club for adults (ages 18+) to discuss children's books. For a list of children's programs at LPL, please check our events calendar.
discovery-0b74cae0507258597a6fead09bb9c1.location: Lancaster Library, LPL Board Room, 151 North Queen Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603

discovery-089be6f3d879a12cf0d878ab1e1c3c.title: McCaskey Combined Choirs – FREE
discovery-089be6f3d879a12cf0d878ab1e1c3c.description: 6:30 pm • Steinman Hall Celebrate the vibrant sound of the J.P. McCaskey High School Combined Choirs in this free concert at the Ware Center in Lancaster. The ensemble, made up of the McCaskey Vocal Ensemble and McCaskey Voices of Freedom, will present a diverse program featuring both accompanied and a cappella choral music. To complement the evening’s art exhibit, the choirs will perform music from African culture, showcasing the students’ versatility and the range of musical styles they study throughout the school year, including both sacred and secular music. As J.P. McCaskey High School approaches its celebration of 90 years of choral music in Lancaster, come support these talented student singers and experience an evening of music, culture, and community. In the Regitz Gallery from 5 to 8 p.m., join us in celebrating the opening of The Places We Go II, a solo exhibition by Ghanaian mixed-media artist Ross Junior Owusu. The exhibit explores migration as an interior and ongoing process of becoming through ceramics, assemblage, and mixed-media artwork. Admission: Free and open to the public! Accessibility: Sensory-friendly accommodations will be available. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more.

discovery-33f0c24b2f08245e3dd06e7b6f5a46.title: Seán Heely’s Celtic Christmas
discovery-33f0c24b2f08245e3dd06e7b6f5a46.description: Saturday, December 5, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Celebrate the season with U.S. National Scottish Fiddle Champion Seán Heely and a cast of nationally acclaimed performers in a festive journey through the Celtic world. Featuring stirring fiddle and bagpipes, dazzling Scottish and Irish dance, and a rich tapestry of Gaelic carols, traditional tunes, and familiar holiday favorites, this joyful production brings Winter Solstice traditions to life with energy and warmth. Tickets: Adults $35 • Students: $25 ASL interpretation, sensory-friendly accommodations, and audio description will be available. Interested? Contact Barry Kornhauser to learn more!

discovery-72a1b4336db32d35c5c9af0307cf17.title: The Hot Sardines – Holiday Stomp
discovery-72a1b4336db32d35c5c9af0307cf17.description: Wednesday, December 9, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Jazz revivalists the Hot Sardines throw a raucous yuletide extravaganza inspired by classic holiday films (such as White Christmas and It’s a Wonderful Life) and timeless classics, with hat-tips to Louis Armstrong, Edith Piaf, Duke Ellington, and beyond. Get your season swinging with fresh takes on “Mistletoe and Holly,” “Le Noël de la Rue,” “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy,” “Blue Christmas,” “Christmas Blues,” “White Christmas,” “Please Come Home for Christmas,” and more. Tickets: Adults $35 • Students: $25

discovery-833f30a513bcd5574ee813bcdc96df.title: Rivers & Big Sky Quartet
discovery-833f30a513bcd5574ee813bcdc96df.description: Friday, December 11, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Atrium Treat yourself to an evening of local folk music that feels like a cozy night around the bonfire. Born out of the simple idea to be able to play anywhere and at any time, Rivers delivers an electrifying indie-folk sound that blends acoustic instrumentation with heart-thumping rhythms. Award-winning folk & roots band Big Sky Quartet weaves an uplifting live show from joyful melodies, glowing three-part harmonies, and truly uplifting energy. Tickets: Adults $15 • Students $15 Accessibility: There will be a pre-show touch tour for blind and low-vision patrons. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more. Presented in partnership with WITF Music.

discovery-f9bbd567adb31829655746f4616ed0.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong Pay-What-You-Want Night
discovery-f9bbd567adb31829655746f4616ed0.description: For these special performances of each production, you may set your own ticket price. A limited number of seats are set aside for this effort as full-price tickets are also sold for these performances. Sales are in person only, no phone calls. Sales start on the day of the Pay-What-You-Want for Mainstage performances at 4 p.m. Note that a line often forms early and must remain outside of the building. We advise checking the weather prior to arrival so that you are prepared to queue outside. Tickets are sold first come – first served on the day of the performance. Limit of 4 tickets per person in line. (Note that full price tickets may be reserved in advance in any quantity.) These policies are subject to change at any time. Be sure to check this page before you arrive at the theatre. Brace yourselves for an awfully big adventure as the accident-prone Cornley Drama Society sets out to present their most audacious production to date. As hilarious as their award-winning The Play That Goes Wrong, Mischief Theatre’s take on J. M. Barrie’s Peter Pan is unforgettable. Something so wrong has never been so right.

discovery-a03924484d3d94e8f22b94f624f605.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong Teen Lounge
discovery-a03924484d3d94e8f22b94f624f605.description: Attend a special behind-the-scenes workshop with professional theatre artists from the current Fulton Theatre Mainstage production. Gain insights about the show and the unique challenges the team faced mounting it. Topics for each Teen Lounge revolve around featured moments from the production such as actors from the show, music, choreography, set design, costumes, and other theatrical design elements. Workshop 5:15PM to 6:15PM. Dinner is on your own. Participants return for the 7:30PM show. Following the performance, a 20-minute post-show Q&A session between actors and the entire audience. This workshop and show combination is just for Teens grades 6-12 and costs only $25! Teen Lounge subscription for the entire season for only $99! Call the Box Office to reserve tickets today: (717) 397-7425. Brace yourselves for an awfully big adventure as the accident-prone Cornley Drama Society sets out to present their most audacious production to date. As hilarious as their award-winning The Play That Goes Wrong, Mischief Theatre’s take on J. M. Barrie’s Peter Pan is unforgettable. Something so wrong has never been so right.

discovery-6b9188293c8c696157d9933de96a13.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong Accessibility Performance
discovery-6b9188293c8c696157d9933de96a13.description: Brace yourselves for an awfully big adventure as the accident-prone Cornley Drama Society sets out to present their most audacious production to date. As hilarious as their award-winning The Play That Goes Wrong, Mischief Theatre’s take on J. M. Barrie’s Peter Pan is unforgettable. Something so wrong has never been so right. ASL Interpretation: Certified interpreters for select performances provide American Sign Language interpretation. To access special reserved seating, complete an Accessibility Ticket Reservation Form. If you need to cancel your reservation, contact access@thefulton.org so that we may extend an offer to wait-listed patrons. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at all ASL interpreted performances. Audio Description is a carefully timed narration of the onstage visual elements in the performance, including the action, costumes, and scenery. Program notes via headset are available 10 to 15 minutes before show time, and a touch tour may be available 1 hour before the show depending on the production (details will be sent via e-mail if a touch tour is available and a separate no-cost reservation will be required). The simultaneous description is broadcast live via an inconspicuous FM receiver. Patrons may choose a single earpiece, dual headset, or a neck loop (for patrons using a hearing aid with a “T” switch), and the device may be used in any seat in the theatre. Patrons may pick up their receiver and headset, free-of-charge, at Audience Services, located in the coat room on the right side of the main lobby. Open-Captioned performances provide patrons with live text presentation of onstage dialogue on a LED screen situated in a box to the right side of the stage. The captions seen on the LED screen may be read from most seats in the theatre, though many prefer seats in the Parquet or Orchestra sections for the best view. An experienced captioner scrolls text in sync with the actors’ spoken word. Tickets can be reserved at the box office or online. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at the open captioned performances listed below. Please fill out the Accessibility Ticket Reservation Form for the Pay-What-You-Want rate for the performances listed.

discovery-209e91d1362c54129161bf67aea464.title: Triple Concerto
discovery-209e91d1362c54129161bf67aea464.description: For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440. Triple Concerto Friday, March 12, 2027: 7:30 PM Saturday, March 13, 2027: 2:30 PM Saturday, March 13, 2027: 7:30 PM Sunday, March 14, 2027: 2:30 PM Join us 45-minutes before each concert for a free pre-concert lecture with Na’Zir McFadden. All four concerts at the Gardner Theatre within Lancaster Country Day School 725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $25-$105 Witness a rare orchestral treasure as three world-class soloists unite for Beethoven's Triple Concerto—violinist Jennifer Frautschi, cellist Zuill Bailey, and pianist Christopher Shih—in an extraordinary conversation between three virtuosos and orchestra. The program opens with Tina Davidson's Bright Air, Brilliant Fire, inspired by ancient philosophy's four elements, and continues with Mendelssohn's beloved "Italian" Symphony, described by the composer as "blue sky in A major" and brimming with Mediterranean sunshine and dance. From elemental fire and Italian light to Beethoven's remarkable three-way dialogue, this concert showcases brilliant soloists in an unforgettable celebration of chamber music on the grandest scale. FEATURING: Na’Zir McFadden, guest conductor Jennifer Frautschi, violinist Zuill Bailey, cellist Christopher Shih, pianist REPERTOIRE: Tina Davidson: Bright Air, Brilliant FireFelix Mendelssohn: Symphony No.4 in A major, op.90 Ludwig van Beethoven: Triple Concerto for Violin, Cello & Piano in C major, op.56 For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440.

discovery-680813b297daed8b58838d22be5bee.description: For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440. Beethoven 9 Friday, May 7, 2027: 7:30 PM Saturday, May 8, 2027: 2:30 PM Saturday, May 8, 2027: 7:30 PM Sunday, May 9, 2027: 2:30 PM Join us 45-minutes before each concert for a free pre-concert lecture with Morihiko Nakahara. All four concerts at the Gardner Theatre within Lancaster Country Day School 725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $25-$105 Join us as we crown our 80th Anniversary Season with one of music's most monumental achievements: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony. This historic finale features the regional premiere of Jeffrey Nytch's powerful Hunger Stones—a contemplative work inspired by ancient climate warnings carved into European riverbeds—and Brahms' joyful Academic Festival Overture, a rousing potpourri of student songs. The evening culminates with Beethoven's revolutionary Ninth Symphony, uniting orchestra, chorus, and vocal soloists in the transcendent "Ode to Joy"—a triumphant celebration of humanity's highest aspirations. From ancient warnings to eternal joy, this season finale honors 80 years of the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra bringing music and community together. discovery-9a331a715a9cbfc8498cff11622cca.title: Ebenezer Scrooges Big Lancaster Christmas Show at Fulton Theater
discovery-9a331a715a9cbfc8498cff11622cca.description: Fast, funny, and full of heart: A Christmas Carol for the 717 The Dickens you know – with a Lancaster twist you’ll love. A streamlined, freewheeling American adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol that sends Scrooge from his childhood in England (at the Burberry Academy for Unloved Boys) to America to make his fortune after being spurned by the love of his life. This Scrooge riffs on the classic story with local references, irreverent humor, homemade magic, and lightning-fast quick changes that astound and delight. The joy of the show is watching a talented, funny cast of five navigate all the lunacy. discovery-64d1703449a860bba31f9f44bc887c.title: Elvis Birthday Bash at American Music Theatre
discovery-64d1703449a860bba31f9f44bc887c.description: Elvis Birthday Bash with Mike Albert & Scot Bruce Mike Albert and Scot Bruce are widely considered the premier Elvis impersonators of our time, performing as the older and younger Elvis, respectively. Mike Albert’s Elvis tribute show has become known worldwide for the respectful portrayal of the late Elvis Presley. Mike has won several major world Elvis contests, and demand for his shows resulted in putting together a seven piece Big “E” Band to emulate the sound Elvis’ band had in the Vegas shows and on tour. Years ago, a part-time “gig” blossomed into a full-time career for Scot Bruce. Because of his uncanny resemblance to the young “King,” along with his ability to sing and strum a guitar, Scot’s live show has taken him all over the world. Scot has had the honor of performing with the legendary Jordanaires, Elvis’ original backup singers. Come experience AMT’s Elvis Birthday Bash and see why audiences are … All Shook Up! discovery-c237e4fc7a5062f59712849d12a543.title: You’ve Still Got a Friend: A Musical Tribute at American Music Theatre
discovery-c237e4fc7a5062f59712849d12a543.description: You’ve Still Got a Friend: A Musical Tribute to the Friendship of Carole King & James Taylor This intimate tribute brings to life the enduring bond between Carole King and James Taylor through the songs that defined a generation. Inspired by their legendary Live at the Troubadour performances and album, this concert weaves together the iconic songs and lived-in performances with the emotional history behind the music. Featured songs include classics like “So Far Away,” “Something in the Way She Moves,” “Sweet Baby James” and “I Feel the Earth Move.” Audiences are invited to step into an evening of timeless songwriting that captures the joy, warmth, and soul of a friendship between two legendary artists who changed music forever. discovery-2c0963a0c08369427caceacb894ba9.title: Reed Timmer at American Music Theatre
discovery-2c0963a0c08369427caceacb894ba9.description: Dominate the Storm: A Heart Pumping Evening with Reed Timmer, America’s Most Famous Storm Chaser Never Stop Chasing! Experience the raw power of nature through the eyes of Dr. Reed Timmer, extreme meteorologist, scientist, and one of the world’s most renowned storm chasers. With a PhD in meteorology from the University of Oklahoma, Reed has devoted his life to intercepting the planet’s most dangerous storms, collecting groundbreaking scientific data, and helping audiences better understand how severe weather is changing. Over the past several decades, Reed has intercepted more than 1,000 tornadoes and 50 hurricanes, including EF5 tornadoes and Category 5 hurricanes. He is also the inventor of the Dominators – armored, tank-like storm-chasing vehicles equipped with advanced meteorological sensors, hydraulic anchoring spikes, drones, probes, balloons, and even model rockets. Since 2020, Reed has driven Dominator 3 directly into 10 tornadoes, more than any other person in history. His unforgettable expeditions include recording 140 mph winds from inside a Nebraska tornado and launching a trackable sensor into a mile-wide EF4 tornado in Kansas. Carried as high as 39,000 feet and reaching speeds of 190 mph, the sensor captured unprecedented data throughout its 30-mile journey inside the vortex. Currently chasing storms for the National Geographic Channel and RadarOmega, Reed also provides vital real-time reports through traditional and social media. Hear the incredible stories, witness breathtaking footage, and discover the science behind Earth’s most powerful storms during this heart-pumping live event. For Reed Timmer, “Never Stop Chasing” is more than a motto – it is a way of life. discovery-970cf0ec51970c5665ecd4250ad9bc.title: Temple Grandin at American Music Theatre
discovery-970cf0ec51970c5665ecd4250ad9bc.description: Dr. Temple Grandin is a world-renowned animal scientist, bestselling author, autism advocate, and one of TIME magazine’s 100 Most Influential People. A professor of animal science at Colorado State University, she revolutionized humane livestock handling and designed systems used throughout the United States and Canada. Diagnosed with severe autism as a child, Dr. Grandin overcame significant challenges to become an influential scientist, educator, and inspirational speaker. Through acclaimed books such as Thinking in Pictures, Animals in Translation, and The Autistic Brain, she has helped millions better understand autism, animal behavior, and the power of thinking differently. Hear the remarkable story, insights, and experiences of a trailblazer whose work continues to transform animal welfare and inspire more inclusive ways of seeing the world. occurrences.title: Temple Grandin at American Music Theatre
occurrences.description: Dr. Temple Grandin is a world-renowned animal scientist, bestselling author, autism advocate, and one of TIME magazine’s 100 Most Influential People. A professor of animal science at Colorado State University, she revolutionized humane livestock handling and designed systems used throughout the United States and Canada. Diagnosed with severe autism as a child, Dr. Grandin overcame significant challenges to become an influential scientist, educator, and inspirational speaker. Through acclaimed books such as Thinking in Pictures, Animals in Translation, and The Autistic Brain, she has helped millions better understand autism, animal behavior, and the power of thinking differently. Hear the remarkable story, insights, and experiences of a trailblazer whose work continues to transform animal welfare and inspire more inclusive ways of seeing the world. discovery-9764e3677919e7ade96d81c2bde691.title: Little River Band at American Music Theatre
discovery-9764e3677919e7ade96d81c2bde691.description: Little River Band with Seals & Crofts 2 The Eagles’ founding member, the late Glenn Frey, knew what he was saying when he dubbed Little River Band “the best singing band in the world.” The current lineup of LRB takes that accolade to heart every time they perform. Through the ‘70s and ‘80s, Little River Band enjoyed huge chart success with multi-platinum albums and chart topping hits like “Reminiscing,” “Cool Change,” “Lonesome Loser,” “The Night Owls,” “Take It Easy On Me,” “Happy Anniversary,” “Lady,” and many more! Experience the timeless harmonies and heartfelt storytelling of Seals & Crofts 2 — a tribute and continuation of the iconic musical legacy of the 1970s soft rock duo, Seals & Crofts. Featuring Brady Seals (cousin of Jim Seals and former member of Little Texas) and Lua Crofts (daughter of Dash Crofts), this dynamic duo brings a fresh and soulful interpretation of the original hits that defined a generation. With voices that echo their legendary family ties and a chemistry that captivates audiences of all ages, Seals & Crofts 2 perform beloved classics like “Summer Breeze,” “Diamond Girl,” and “We May Never Pass This Way (Again),” alongside new original music that honors the spirit and sincerity of the originals. More than just a tribute, Seals & Crofts 2 is a celebration of musical heritage, connection, and the enduring power of melody. Don’t miss this enchanting evening filled with nostalgia, harmony, and artistry that bridges generations. discovery-413227471a681ff11baf48e8b09484.title: TUSK: The Classic Tribute to Fleetwood Mac at American Music Theatre
discovery-413227471a681ff11baf48e8b09484.description: Tusk is the number one Tribute to Fleetwood Mac in the world. No fancy tricks, no gimmicks, just five musicians recreating the music of Fleetwood Mac to perfection with note for note renditions that no other Fleetwood Mac tribute on the touring scene today can come close to duplicating. Tusk covers all the great hits of Fleetwood Mac. The five musicians comprising Tusk have been making music together in various combinations and styles for over 25 years. Authentic-sounding and always respectful, Tusk leaves no stone unturned in replicating the sounds of one of the world’s best-loved, top-selling bands. discovery-f78029b16e83e4ec70bc463ed88e8e.title: Local Author Book Fair
discovery-f78029b16e83e4ec70bc463ed88e8e.description: Support local writers and explore stories from your own community at the Library's 2nd annual Local Author Book Fair! Just in time for the holiday season, Lancaster Public Library will host the Local Author Book Fair on Saturday, December 12, from 10AM - 1PM in the library's 1st floor combined Community Room and Boardroom. Stop by the library to meet local authors and hear about the books they have written. Books will be available for sale and signing by the authors. Are you a local author? Authors from the Lancaster-area who have either traditionally or self-published books for adults, teens, or children in any genre are eligible to register for the Book Fair. Space is limited, but preference will be given to the first 10 authors to complete the registration form. https://bit.ly/3WrONyc

discovery-716b4a7ba82e0df3e45379c1a400f0.title: Crafternoon at MTPL: Traditional German Paper Stars⭐
discovery-716b4a7ba82e0df3e45379c1a400f0.description: Unwind and embrace a classic holiday crafting tradition! Join us at the library to learn the art of weaving and folding 3D German paper stars (also known as Fröbelsterne). Using four paper strips and a series of clever folds, you'll transform flat paper into intricate, eye-catching stars perfect for holiday tree ornaments, gift toppers, or festive window decorations. Whether you are an experienced paper crafter or completely new to the fold, step-by-step guidance will be provided. All paper and supplies are included-- just bring your patience and creativity!
discovery-716b4a7ba82e0df3e45379c1a400f0.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center A, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-127f295614114176589b0a69e87eb0.title: Small Talk: A Novella Book Club
discovery-127f295614114176589b0a69e87eb0.description: Small books. Big conversations. 2nd Saturdays from 2:30-3:30. Most book clubs are a marathon-- this is a sprint! We exclusively read books under 300 pages: perfect for the busy reader who wants all the discussion without the 500-page commitment. Join us for sharp conversation that's short, sweet, and gets straight to the point! discovery-99c54312708cd2896d20b4041f6c0f.title: Kept Like a Secret by Kendyll Hillegas
discovery-99c54312708cd2896d20b4041f6c0f.description: February 5 to 26 • Regitz Gallery Opening reception: Friday, February 5, 2027 • 5-8 PM A glowing ear. Yellow leaves. An untethered kite. These images have persisted in Kendyll Hillegas’ awareness since childhood, like intermittent visual background noise. They appear without warning, often precipitating a cascade of emotion the artist calls The Feeling—a sudden longing, an acute awareness of time, an intense desire to know and be known. Through colorful oil paintings, Kept Like a Secret is Hillegas’ attempt to paint The Feeling by chasing the images that summon it, turning up the volume on the background noise and seeing where it leads. About the Artist Kendyll Hillegas is an award-winning illustrator and fine artist known for technical and emotional realism. Over the past decade, she has collaborated with clients including Coca-Cola, A24 Films, and Vanity Fair on a wide range of commercial and editorial projects. Her recent body of oil paintings expands on the precise, vivid realism she is known for as an illustrator, adding new layers of narrative complexity through landscape, large-scale portraits, and close-cropped figurative compositions. She exhibited her debut solo show “Kept Like a Secret” at The Gallery at St. Mary’s, Manhattan, in late 2025. She holds a BFA in Painting and works from her studio in York, Pennsylvania.

discovery-fb8cf270f39e53c3ce43d913d58554.title: The Places We Go II by Ross Junior Owusu
discovery-fb8cf270f39e53c3ce43d913d58554.description: December 4–January 29 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, December 4, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. Artist Talk: 6 p.m. The Places We Go II is a solo exhibition by Ghanaian mixed-media artist Ross Junior Owusu exploring migration as an interior and ongoing process of becoming. Through ceramics, assemblage, and mixed-media artwork, Owusu examines how memory, resilience, cultural identity, and belonging are carried, reshaped, and rebuilt across shifting landscapes. Using fragmented materials such as clay and reclaimed objects, Owusu presents migration not as a fixed journey of loss or arrival, but as a layered negotiation of selfhood. His sculptural works reflect the physical and emotional imprints of movement, exploring what is carried forward, what is left behind, and what endures. Clay serves as a central material and metaphor in Owusu’s practice, reflecting cycles of becoming, un-becoming, and re-becoming. His sculptural forms draw from West African visual languages, including textured surfaces and modular interpretations of Krobo bead structures, while referencing architecture, the human body, and emotional landscapes. Reclaimed bicycle parts and earthy surface treatments further evoke movement, resilience, transformation, and connection to place. Through repetition, assemblage, texture, and vibrant surface treatments, The Places We Go II invites viewers to consider how identity is continually shaped and reshaped by movement, memory, place, and relationships. The exhibition features approximately 10 works exploring the complex connections between cultural heritage and evolving environments. About the Artist Ross Junior Owusu is a Ghanaian mixed-media artist and educator working across ceramics, performance, and assemblage. He holds an MFA in Studio Art with a concentration in Ceramics from Wayne State University and a BA in Industrial Art with a concentration in Ceramics from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Ghana. He currently serves as an Assistant Professor of Art at Talladega College. Owusu’s artistic practice explores identity, migration, and cultural memory, examining how identities are carried, negotiated, and reassembled across changing geographies. His work combines contemporary mixed-media practices with West African visual languages, creating sculptural forms that connect inherited traditions with personal experience and contemporary environments.

discovery-9e1a54696f539628fb20cacac00146.title: Overshare: I Did This for Me by Shauna L Yorty
discovery-9e1a54696f539628fb20cacac00146.description: November 6–24 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, November 6, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. Artist Talk: 6 p.m. Overshare: I Did This for Me is a raw, intimate body of work by Lancaster-based artist Shauna L Yorty, created over three years of survival, transformation, and self-discovery. Through cardboard collages and mixed media artwork, including dimensional pieces, Yorty explores the messy, hopeful, and deeply personal process of making art as a means of moving through difficult experiences. Yorty describes the exhibition as a culmination of three years of “survival, process, and expression in service of love.” The works are made from humble, everyday materials and embrace an intentionally raw, handmade aesthetic. Bright colors, bold forms, layered textures, and dimensional elements transform discarded materials into expressive works of contemporary art. Rather than creating art for perfection or approval, Yorty makes art as a way to process, connect, and keep moving forward. Overshare: I Did This for Me invites viewers to consider their own stories, vulnerabilities, and creative processes, while finding connection with others through artistic expression. About the Artist Shauna L Yorty is a Lancaster-based artist whose bright, bold artwork tells powerful stories of hope and healing. occurrences.title: Overshare: I Did This for Me by Shauna L Yorty
occurrences.description: November 6–24 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, November 6, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. Artist Talk: 6 p.m. Overshare: I Did This for Me is a raw, intimate body of work by Lancaster-based artist Shauna L Yorty, created over three years of survival, transformation, and self-discovery. Through cardboard collages and mixed media artwork, including dimensional pieces, Yorty explores the messy, hopeful, and deeply personal process of making art as a means of moving through difficult experiences. Yorty describes the exhibition as a culmination of three years of “survival, process, and expression in service of love.” The works are made from humble, everyday materials and embrace an intentionally raw, handmade aesthetic. Bright colors, bold forms, layered textures, and dimensional elements transform discarded materials into expressive works of contemporary art. Rather than creating art for perfection or approval, Yorty makes art as a way to process, connect, and keep moving forward. discovery-e2020a2ba79dac3c4905a3983097ab.title: SOLD OUT – Glorious Sounds of the Season
discovery-e2020a2ba79dac3c4905a3983097ab.description: This performance is sold out. This is the 21st annual performance of Glorious Sounds of the Season, a festive fundraiser presented by over 250 students and faculty from MU’s Tell School of Music. Proceeds support student scholarships and program development. Traditional holiday favorites are presented alongside a diverse and varied selection of world music. To create musical momentum and excitement, the concert is presented in a unique kaleidoscopic format. Performers are placed throughout the hall — with no applause between selections — creating seamless transitions and continuous music-making. This Millersville tradition is the perfect way to get into the holiday spirit! Be sure to purchase your tickets early, as performances often sell out. Ticket PricesAdvanced: $30.00 Day Of: $34.00 MU Student w/ID: $5.00* *MU Students will receive up to one (1) discounted ticket with a valid MU ID. MU discounts are NOT available online and must be made in-person or by calling any box office location. MU discount tickets are subject to availability on the day of the event.Advanced ticket reservations are strongly encouraged.

Tickets: Adults $65 • Students: $55 Stay tuned for details about a VIP reception!

discovery-b898c186fb9072c4700d85bdf93b81.title: LBBB presents “Our Best Brass Christmas”
discovery-b898c186fb9072c4700d85bdf93b81.description: Sunday, December 20 • 3:00 PM • Steinman Hall Lancaster British Brass Band consists of 31 players. It draws its personnel from the four state regions of Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware and New Jersey. Originally conceived as a top-level, professional quality ensemble, it includes among its membership professional solo and ensemble players and music teacher/performers. The band members bring years of playing and teaching experience to the organization from such diverse institutions as The United States Marine Band, and the Lancaster, Harrisburg, Reading and York Symphony Orchestras. Many players are currently engaged as teachers in various public and private school venues and in such institutions of higher learning as West Chester, Millersville and Kutztown Universities, Lebanon Valley College, and The University of Delaware. Tickets: $25

discovery-355465fc912456bd8f95cf74e1cec5.title: Mixtape: Ali Murphy & Joshua William Green
discovery-355465fc912456bd8f95cf74e1cec5.description: For years, Ali Murphy has led from the keys at the heart of Prima’s most iconic experiences. As pianist and music director of ILLUMINATION and numerous other productions, she has shaped the emotional architecture of the room with precision and artistry. Joshua William Green brings rich baritone depth and unmistakable presence. A frequent Prima director who steps into the spotlight when called, he carries both musical craftsmanship and warmth. Together, they curate a mixtape of songs that influenced their journeys — revealing the roots behind the sound audiences have come to love. Purchase individual tickets for each Mixtape performance, or bundle with the February Mixtape show and purchase a subscription to save! Get tickets Get Mixtape Subscription For Mixtape Concerts, libations are available for purchase at the in-theater bar. Stay in the loop: Sign up for Prima emails and be the first to know when tickets drop!

discovery-d0882298bc655770cbafaa3711e704.title: Crazy Little Thing Called Love
discovery-d0882298bc655770cbafaa3711e704.description: Part concert. Part comedy. Way more fun than couples therapy. Classic pop-rock favorites burst to life, woven with intimate, cabaret-style moments where performers share funny, heartfelt stories about love — the kind that will have you laughing one minute and leaning a little closer to the person beside you the next. A powerhouse band fuels iconic anthems with electric sing-along energy, while those in-between moments make it feel personal and quite playful. It’s fresh and yet nostalgic — a celebration of love in all its forms and phases — steady, surprising, hard-earned, and deeply felt… in a concert experience that’ll leave you glowing. discovery-d645917fcf1fdf9cecbee8a0aec15b.title: Mitch Nugent: The Founder’s Mixtape
discovery-d645917fcf1fdf9cecbee8a0aec15b.description: For the first time in a decade, Prima’s Founding Executive Producer steps into the light with a deeply personal mixtape. Stories never shared publicly. Moments that formed the man behind the mission. The songs and crossroads that shaped fifteen years of Prima. This is not a retrospective. It is a reveal. Purchase individual tickets for each Mixtape performance, or bundle with the January Mixtape show and purchase a subscription to save! GET TICKETS Get Mixtape Subscription For Mixtape Concerts, libations are available for purchase at the in-theater bar. Stay in the loop: Sign up for Prima emails and be the first to know when tickets drop!

discovery-16156ab56c631153ac2b215fa468ad.title: Play with a Play
discovery-16156ab56c631153ac2b215fa468ad.description: Rob Bell’s next play is taking shape. Pull up a chair. Hear selected scenes. Join Rob in conversation. Help a new story find its voice. Professional actors will read selected scenes from the next exciting play, followed by an intimate conversation with Rob and the performers. These excerpts offer an early glimpse of the work ahead of its fully staged world premiere at Prima in 2028. Ask questions. Share what surprises you, moves you, or leaves you wanting more. Together, we’ll explore the possibilities and breathe life into something new. It’s an invitation to be among the first inside the making of a new play, with a place in the dialogue that helps it grow. Subscribe to the 2026-2027 season now to secure the best seats and save over $80! First access for Prima subscribers, donors, and sponsors. Any remaining tickets may be released to the public at a later date.For Prima subscribers, Play with a Play is included as your final experience of the season. discovery-514df60a5e4aa1f1e2d1a2c60a8794.title: Demuth 101
discovery-514df60a5e4aa1f1e2d1a2c60a8794.description: November 30 & December 7, 6 - 7:30 pm | Ages 16+ This art history course will provide students with an introduction to Charles Demuth-- his life and his artwork. We will begin with exploring Demuth’s roots and early life in Lancaster, and follow his travels as he moved through the Modern Art world - forging famous friendships and pioneering the Precisionism movement. The class will take an in-depth look at examples of Demuth’s artwork and discuss how they fit within the scope of American Modernism and the impact he had on art history. Some out of class work will be required. Co-teachers are Abby Baer, Executive Director, and Greta Rymar, Exhibitions & Collections Manager. Combined they have over 18 years of experience working at the museum and studying Demuth. Price: $60 members, $75 non-members. Register→
discovery-514df60a5e4aa1f1e2d1a2c60a8794.location: Demuth Program Center, 116 East King Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602

discovery-a044020f5275d1e38f332dd823df4c.title: Seen / Reseen: Recursive Photographs by Richard K Kent
discovery-a044020f5275d1e38f332dd823df4c.description: Recursion, whether in mathematics or in visual phenomena, relies on a function or an image that is repeated to yield a new iteration, which then in turn is repeated. Subsequent iterations build on one another, but always yield something new that reflects what has come before. By undergoing this recursive process, Kent’s photographic iterations capture both rural and urban landscapes, visually documenting the passage of time. Image: Richard K Kent, New Holland & Franklin, 1st Series, 5X, archival pigment print

discovery-ecbc22ddc2ba33240c63c2f5bb6049.title: Come From Away
discovery-ecbc22ddc2ba33240c63c2f5bb6049.description: Based on the remarkable true story that took place in an isolated community, Come From Away is a critically acclaimed musical featuring an enduringly relevant script accompanied by a deeply moving score by Irene Sankoff and David Hein. What began as an average day in the town of Gander, Newfoundland, turned into an international sleepover when 38 planes, carrying thousands of people from around the globe, were diverted to Gander’s airstrip on September 11, 2001. Undaunted by culture clashes and language barriers, the people of Gander welcomed the stranded travelers with music, an open bar, and the recognition that we’re all part of a global family. Content Guide

discovery-cd4dd1428bf7c59419b62c69868ed7.description: Eliza Doolittle is a young flower seller with an unmistakable Cockney accent, which keeps her in the lower rungs of Edwardian society. discovery-b411305d86374922d57dd9705eac26.title: Ebenezer Scrooge's Big Lancaster Christmas Show
discovery-b411305d86374922d57dd9705eac26.description: The Dickens you know—with a Lancaster twist you’ll love. A streamlined, freewheeling American adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol that sends Scrooge from his childhood in England (at the Burberry Academy for Unloved Boys) to America to make his fortune after being spurned by the love of his life. This Scrooge riffs on the classic story with local references, irreverent humor, homemade magic, and lightning-fast quick changes that astound and delight. The joy of the show is watching a talented, funny cast of five navigate all the lunacy. The Groff Studio Series is performed in our 4th Floor Tell Studio Theatre and is designed for General Admission Seating Ebenezer Scrooge’s Big Lancaster Christmas Show General Seating Layout *does not reflect actual number of seats Content Guide

discovery-d7a3efee18c3a35b01ea0dc761f2c2.title: A Streetcar Named Desire
discovery-d7a3efee18c3a35b01ea0dc761f2c2.description: Winner! 1948 Pulitzer Prize for Drama Winner! 1948 Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play (Jessica Tandy) Winner! Three 2023 Olivier Awards, including Best Revival of a Play After losing her Mississippi home to creditors, Blanche DuBois relocates to the New Orleans home of her younger sister and brother-in-law, Stella and Stanley Kowalski. Undermined by romantic illusions, Blanche is unable to cope with life’s harsh realities. Though she finds a glimmer of hope while connecting with Stanley’s gentlemanly friend, Mitch, Blanche cannot face the truth of her own troubled past and ultimately descends into madness. The Groff Studio Series is performed in our 4th Floor Tell Studio Theatre and is designed for General Admission Seating Content Guide

discovery-284711072d38f339d71fdaccfcd7ad.title: 'Twas The Night Before Christmas

discovery-a7c00aae42890dfd3d0a6a53cfc0ec.title: Honk! JR
discovery-a7c00aae42890dfd3d0a6a53cfc0ec.description: Ages 10-16 This production is currently at capacity. Sign Up For The Waitlist The beloved tale of Hans Christian Andersen’s The Ugly Duckling bursts into song in this charming musical adaptation about navigating our differences and finding where we belong. In Honk JR, Ugly isn’t quite like his darling duckling brothers and sisters—and he soon finds out that standing out in his barnyard world isn’t easy! When Ugly finds himself separated from his family, he sets out on an adventure filled with colorful new friendships, a conniving cat, and the discovery that what makes him different is also what makes him special! Bursting with color and fun, Honk JR is perfect for audiences of all ages! auditions December 7-8 held at Lancaster Alliance Church Following enrollment, all registered students should sign up for a 5-minute audition slot, which helps the production team play to everyone’s strengths in the distribution of roles and other show material. More details about auditions are included in the Welcome Letter sent about two months prior to the start of rehearsals. Rehearsal Schedule January 3-17 at Lancaster Alliance Church (210 Pitney Rd, Lancaster) January 18-21 at Smoketown Elementary School (500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster) 6-9pm Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays 3-9pm Sundays Performances Performances take place at Smoketown Elementary School (500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster, PA 17602). Friday, January 22 | 7pmSaturday, January 23 | 11am & 3pmSunday, January 24 | 3pm Approximate run-time is an hour and 15 minutes. No intermission. Tickets are Pay-What-You-Will and all donations help support Servant Stage's Youth Theatre program! Info on Tuition/Financial Aid See our Tiered Pricing Options. A non-refundable $25 fee is required for initial registration. Within a week of your enrollment, you will receive instructions to make full tuition payment and complete your registration through the new Servant Stage portal. Payment will be due by November 15. No refunds will be issued within one month of the start of camp (December 3). Youth Theatre Production costs include: T-shirt, all materials and handouts, rehearsals with the Servant Stage staff. If you need to apply for financial assistance, you can do so here. Additional Information Students will need to bring their own snacks, dinners, and water bottles. All students who register are expected to be able to attend all rehearsals and performances. Meet the Directors Danielle PoznanovicDirector HONK JR is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.MTIShows.com. back to Youth Theatre Home Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. discovery-c4df4e17b0c9fa05096eeb52bbdbcb.title: Frozen
discovery-c4df4e17b0c9fa05096eeb52bbdbcb.description: JANUARY 3 - February 7 PERFORMANCE SCHEDULE Smoketown Elementary School 500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster Friday, January 29 • 7pm Saturday, January 30 • 11am & 3pm Sunday, January 31 • 3pm Friday, February 5 • 7pm Saturday, February 6 • 11am & 3pm Sunday, February 7 • 3pm Servant Stage is proud to present an all-teen production of Disney’s Frozen, the full-length Broadway musical based on the beloved animated film, featuring music and lyrics by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez and a book by Jennifer Lee. This magical and heartfelt musical tells the story of sisters Anna and Elsa, whose deep bond is tested when Elsa’s hidden powers plunge the kingdom of Arendelle into an eternal winter. As Anna sets out on a daring journey to bring her sister home, she encounters the rugged Kristoff, his loyal reindeer Sven, and the delightfully optimistic snowman Olaf. Featuring beloved songs including “Let It Go,” “For the First Time in Forever,” and “Do You Want to Build a Snowman?” alongside new music written for the stage, Frozen is an adventurous and moving story of family, courage, self-acceptance, and the extraordinary power of love. Program & Production Information Teen Productions These shows are full-length musicals for teen performers (ages 13-19). These productions are for experienced students who are ready to engage with material that is lengthier and more complex. Unlike our JR and KIDS productions, where registration takes place before auditions, these productions will be cast fully by auditions, with auditions taking place well in advance of the rehearsal process. Upon receiving casting offers, students will register with tuition following our tiered pricing model. The cast size is slightly smaller than our JR and KIDS cast sizes, allowing for more focused intentional work with the students, a more efficient rehearsal process, and more opportunities for students to take on understudy and swing responsibilities. Similarly to our JR productions this will be a more realised production with a small set, curated props, costumes, and lights to visually support the work of the students. Content Advisory Disney’s Frozen is a full-length stage adaptation of the beloved Disney animated film, featuring the familiar characters, story, and songs alongside additional music written for the stage. Themes of grief and loss, including the death of Anna and Elsa’s parents. Moments of mild peril and violence, including characters being threatened, injured, or placed in life-threatening situations. Some potentially frightening or emotionally intense moments involving Elsa’s magical powers, isolation, and fear. Meet the DIRECTOR Lauren SchaefferDirector All shows are Pay-What-You-Will in keeping with Servant Stage's mission to make exceptional performances accessible to everyone. You are welcome to donate by cash, check, or credit card at the performance, or online or by mail at any time. Thank you for your support that makes the mission of Servant Stage possible! back to youth theatre home Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. The advertised range is not a continuous performance.

discovery-0bc381ff704dc265f4c98ad6777fee.title: Forever Plaid
discovery-0bc381ff704dc265f4c98ad6777fee.description: March 18 - April 25 Tickets Coming Soon Get ready for a heavenly helping of harmony with Forever Plaid—the beloved musical comedy that celebrates the timeless magic of four-part harmony! When four aspiring singers are given one final chance to perform together, they’ll stop at nothing to make their dreams come true. Packed with unforgettable songs, hilarious mishaps, and plenty of heart, Forever Plaid is a nostalgic trip through the golden age of pop music. With tight harmonies, charming choreography, and a cast you’ll instantly adore, this feel-good favorite is a celebration of friendship, music, and the enduring power of a dream. All shows are Pay-What-You-Will in keeping with Servant Stage's mission to make exceptional performances accessible to everyone. You are welcome to donate by cash, check, or credit card at the performance, or online or by mail at any time. Thank you for your support that makes the mission of Servant Stage possible! Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. The advertised range is not a continuous performance.

discovery-b200267b031441513802e40fa9350a.title: Once Upon A Mattress: Youth Edition
discovery-b200267b031441513802e40fa9350a.description: Ages 13-18 This camp is currently at capacity. sign up for the waitlist Many moons ago in a far-off place, Queen Aggravain decreed no couples could marry until her son, Prince Dauntless, found a bride. Now the Prince is a young man and princesses from far and wide attempt to win his hand in marriage. None can pass the impossible tests given to them by the Queen until the “shy” swamp princess, Winnifred the Woebegone, shows up. Will she be able to pass the Sensitivity Test, marry her prince, and help Lady Larken and Sir Harry to the altar? Carried on a wave of wonderful songs, by turns hilarious and raucous, romantic and melodic, this rollicking spin on the classic tale “The Princess and the Pea” provides some side-splitting shenanigans and proves that a genuine princess is exceedingly rare! auditions Auditions will take place on the first afternoon of rehearsal, Sunday, April 4th from 3-6pm. All registered students participate in auditions, which help the production team play to everyone’s strengths in the distribution of roles and other show material. More details about auditions are included in the Welcome Letter sent about two months prior to the start of rehearsals. Rehearsal Schedule April 4-24 at Lancaster Alliance Church (210 Pitney Rd, Lancaster) April 25-29 at Smoketown Elementary School (500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster) 3-9pm on Sundays 6-9pm Tuesdays, Thursdays, & Wednesday, April 28 Performances Performances take place at Smoketown Elementary School (500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster, PA 17602). Friday, April 30 | 7pmSaturday, May 1 | 11am & 3pmSunday, May 2 | 3pm Approximate run-time is an hour and 15 minutes. No intermission. Tickets are Pay-What-You-Will and all donations help support Servant Stage's Youth Theatre program! Info on Tuition/Financial Aid See our Tiered Pricing Options. A non-refundable $25 fee is required for initial registration. Within a week of your enrollment, you will receive instructions to make full tuition payment and complete your registration through the new Servant Stage portal. Payment will be due by December 15. No refunds will be issued within one month of the start of camp (March 4). Youth Theatre Production costs include: T-shirt, all materials and handouts, and rehearsals with the Servant Stage staff. If you need to apply for financial assistance, you can do so here. Additional Information Students will need to bring their own snacks, dinners, and water bottles. All students who register are expected to be able to attend all rehearsals and performances. Meet the Directors Sierra NaomiDirector ONCE UPON A MATTRESS: YOUTH EDITION is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals. www.concordtheatricals.com back to Youth Theatre Home Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. The advertised range is not a continuous performance.

discovery-6c70a56c4ef160fc690fab51b55c27.title: Disney's Winnie the Pooh KIDS
discovery-6c70a56c4ef160fc690fab51b55c27.description: Ages 8-12 This camp is currently at capacity. sign up for the waitlist Welcome to the Hundred Acre Wood, where Winnie the Pooh is once again in search of honey. Along the way, he meets his pals, Tigger, Piglet, Rabbit and Owl, but soon discovers that Christopher Robin has been captured by the mysterious Backson! As they prepare for a rescue operation, the animals learn about teamwork, friendship and, of course... sharing snacks. Disney's Winnie the Pooh KIDS is a delightful show based on the beloved characters of A.A. Milne and the 2011 Disney animated feature film. Featuring favorite songs from the film, as well as new hits by the Academy Award-winning Robert and Kristen Lopez (Frozen), this honey-filled delight is as sweet as it is fun! auditions Auditions will take place on the first night of rehearsal, Tuesday, April 6 from 6-9pm. All registered students participate in auditions, which help the production team play to everyone’s strengths in the distribution of roles and other show material. More details about auditions are included in the Welcome Letter sent about two months prior to the start of rehearsals. Rehearsal Schedule April 6 - May 8 at Lancaster Alliance Church (210 Pitney Rd, Lancaster) 6-8:30pm Tuesdays & Thursdays & Friday, May 7 Students will be called at 10am for a final dress rehearsal on Saturday, May 8. *Note the later end time (9pm) for the first rehearsal/auditions on April 6* Performances Performances take place at Lancaster Alliance Church (210 Pitney Rd, Lancaster) Saturday, May 8 | 1pm & 4pm Approximate run-time is 35 minutes. No intermission. Tickets are Pay-What-You-Will and all donations help support Servant Stage's Youth Theatre program! Info on Tuition/Financial Aid See our Tiered Pricing Options. A non-refundable $25 fee is required for initial registration. Within a week of your enrollment, you will receive instructions to make full tuition payment and complete your registration through the new Servant Stage portal. Payment will be due by December 15. No refunds will be issued within one month of the start of rehearsal (March 6). Youth Theatre Production costs include: T-shirt, all materials and handouts, and rehearsals with the Servant Stage staff. If you need to apply for financial assistance, you can do so here. Additional Information Students will need to bring their own snacks, dinners, and water bottles. All students who register are expected to be able to attend all rehearsals and performances. DISNEY’S WINNIE THE POOH KIDS is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.MTIShows.com. back to Youth Theatre Home Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. discovery-73f4011784ed9dedb0001f657698c6.description: May 21 - June 13 Tickets Coming Soon Step into a world of magic with Mary Poppins—the beloved musical filled with unforgettable songs, dazzling moments, and a spoonful of imagination! When the Banks family welcomes a mysterious new nanny into their home, ordinary life takes flight in the most extraordinary ways. Featuring timeless favorites like “A Spoonful of Sugar,” “Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious,” and “Step in Time,” Mary Poppins is a joyful celebration of family, adventure, and the magic of seeing the world a little differently. With spectacular dancing, memorable characters, and heartwarming moments for all ages, this practically perfect musical will delight audiences from beginning to end! All shows are Pay-What-You-Will in keeping with Servant Stage's mission to make exceptional performances accessible to everyone. discovery-95c47feac732c1e2634cbb01a1cc48.description: July 9 - August 15 Tickets Coming Soon Join Charlie Brown and the whole Peanuts gang for You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown—a charming musical celebration of the joys, frustrations, and adventures of childhood! From Lucy’s big opinions and Schroeder’s love of Beethoven to Snoopy’s flights of fancy and Charlie Brown’s eternal quest for a little good luck, this beloved classic brings Charles Schulz’s iconic characters to life with humor, heart, and plenty of memorable music. Filled with catchy songs, playful choreography, and moments that are sure to make audiences smile, You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown reminds us that sometimes the simplest things—and the people we share them with—are what make life special. discovery-6ac1d0cf2d2cc4e93df4cca23b2d7a.description: NovEMBER 5 - DecEMBER 19 tickets coming soon Celebrate the most wonderful time of the year with Christmas Crooners—a heartwarming and nostalgic holiday revue filled with timeless music, festive fun, and plenty of Christmas cheer! Journey back to the golden age of holiday entertainment as a talented ensemble brings beloved carols, classic Christmas favorites, and fresh takes on familiar tunes to life. From tender ballads to toe-tapping favorites, Christmas Crooners captures the warmth, joy, and wonder of the season with soaring harmonies, dazzling performances, and a healthy dose of holiday sparkle. Perfect for the whole family, this festive celebration will have you singing along, smiling from ear to ear, and ready to celebrate Christmas! All shows are Pay-What-You-Will in keeping with Servant Stage's mission to make exceptional performances accessible to everyone. You are welcome to donate by cash, check, or credit card at the performance, or online or by mail at any time. Thank you for your support that makes the mission of Servant Stage possible! Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. The advertised range is not a continuous performance.

discovery-d87d8e056e2d1bb12608266b059252.description: Friday November 27th, 2026 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $23.40 + Fees Reserved Riser Seating | $34.70 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Big Fan Presents ————————————————— Shakedown Citi is a fresh new force on the jam band scene, born in the heart of a Grateful Dead parking lot at Citi Field in 2023. When the band’s members crossed paths on Shakedown Street, something clicked – and the music hasn’t stopped since. Rather than imitating the Dead, Shakedown Citi channels their spirit – creating spontaneous, soulful performances that feel alive, adventurous and totally in the moment. Each set is a journey, full of unexpected twists, deep grooves and musical conversation that pulls even the most skeptical listener into the vibe. Every Shakedown Citi show begins long before the first note. Each setlist is thoughtfully and meticulously crafted from the Dead repertoire, affiliated catalogs and beyond, balancing deep cuts and beloved anthems, rarities and reprises. No two nights are ever the same – each performance stands as a work of art on its own, alive in its moment, while also fitting into the larger patchwork of the repertoire. It’s not just a tribute – it’s the Dead, reborn. Check out Shakedown Citi here! discovery-e95a8227bf96b5ff1082bf20036729.description: Saturday November 28th, 2026 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $29.55 + Fees Reserved Balcony & Mezzanine Seating | $40.30 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Big Fan Presents ————————————————— The Small Town Titans return to Mickey’s Black Box for their annual Home Town Holiday Show! The Small Town Titans are an American rock n’ roll power trio from York, PA who love to constantly create, as well as play live. Gone is the notion that a rock band should only release 10 songs at a time every 2 years. In a world where music fans crave new content constantly, the Small Town Titans aim to deliver their brand of art all of the time, drawing inspiration from a newer wave of rock bands such as Highly Suspect and Royal Blood, and rock legends such as the Foo Fighters, Audioslave, and Deep Purple. Thanks to their efforts at taking matters into their own hands, STT can create and release songs, podcasts, live online concerts, and more with no rules. In a social media driven world, STT knows releasing quality, constant content is as important as playing great live shows. In November of 2018, the band’s cover of the Christmas song “You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch” went viral in a matter of days, leading to charting on various Billboard charts including Holiday Digital Song Sales, Rock Digital Song Sales, Emerging Artists, and reaching #5 on the Next Big Sound chart. The song also reached #2 on the iTunes Rock charts, only being surpassed by Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody”. STT quickly found themselves achieving success, all on their own terms. As a continued unsigned act, all three members have risen to the occasion to continue to make music the way they want to, free from having to follow traditional music industry rules. By changing their mindset and focus towards creating content like many successful YouTubers, STT has made fans the old fashioned way, by word of mouth. With no manager, label, or radio support, the Small Town Titans have managed to find success by simply never forgetting one thing, their fans, both new and old. Instead of trying to make a million fans, STT is focusing on the fans they already have, and the ones they continue to make. With a love for playing live, a Small Town Titans show has evolved into more than a concert. It’s an event, with a set list that’s decided right before the show, and plenty of stage banter in between songs. The band simply hits the stage to deliver an energy driven show using guitars, drums, and their voices. Nothing more, nothing less. This approach to their live performances has led to them sharing the stage with acts such as Highly Suspect, Papa Roach, Black Stone Cherry, Pop Evil, and more. Check out the Small Town Titans here! discovery-46dbc85f36113086538907f5d26b0c.description: Saturday December 5th, 2026 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $32.65 + Fees Reserved Balcony & Mezzanine Seating | $37.75 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases Please note this event is 21+ – Valid ID Required to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box ————————————————– It is a little-known fact that most Amish practice a tradition similar to the Christian “Confirmation” and Jewish “Bar Mitzvah” called “Rumspringa” (literal translation: “running around”) in which Amish children at the age of 16 have an opportunity to live free of the strict Amish code of conduct before deciding if they want to come back and be baptized into the Amish church. Surprisingly, virtually all of the youths return. But sometimes they don’t. Four out of the original six members of The Amish Outlaws were born and raised in Lancaster, PA and had a strict Amish upbringing. No electricity from land lines, no alcohol, no musical instruments, but their spirits were too wild for the Amish lifestyle. Once they trampled in the Devil’s Playground, there was no turning back. In the years since Rumspringa, the members of the Amish Outlaws have become very well acclimated to the pleasures and vices of the modern world… music, most of all. Hip hop, rock, country, metal, disco, opera. There is no genre they do not touch upon. Thus, with a bold lust for life and a fire for music and performance that can only come from 16 years of repression, The Amish Outlaws were unleashed upon the world. Not for The Early November, however. Ever since forming in New Jersey in 2001, the band, now consisting of frontman Ace Enders and founding drummer Jeff Kummer— have constantly been striving to find the best and most definitive version of themselves. With this self-titled record, the seventh studio album of their career, the duo have come as close as is possible to doing so. It’s an album that ties the past, present and future all together, and as such, it marks what Enders calls a “period or exclamation point in our sentence”. It’s not a new beginning, per se, but nevertheless something emphatic that signifies, in Enders’ words again, “a pivotal moment” for them both. Check out The Early November here! discovery-d0f5cb22f69e0c868e368a51050780.title: BLURRYFACE: A Full-Production Tribute to Twenty One Pilots
discovery-d0f5cb22f69e0c868e368a51050780.description: Friday January 8th, 2027 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $35.70 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box ————————————————– BLURRYFACE is a tribute to Twenty One Pilots built by fans, for fans. Designed to capture the energy, emotion, and spectacle of a full Twenty One Pilots concert, BLURRYFACE delivers an up-close and personal live experience crafted specifically for intimate venues where the original band cultivated their passionate fanbase. Audiences get the rare feeling of being fully immersed in the music, the visuals, and the community that has made Twenty One Pilots one of modern music’s most dedicated fanbases. This is far more than a cover set. BLURRYFACE recreates the feeling of a modern Twenty One Pilots arena production inside a smaller, more personal environment. Featuring synchronized video content, dynamic lighting, programmed visuals, CO2 cannons, and carefully curated live moments, every aspect of the show is designed to capture the emotional highs, explosive energy, and atmosphere fans know and love. From massive singalongs to intimate moments of reflection, the goal is to make every audience member feel like they are part of something bigger than just a concert. At its core, BLURRYFACE exists to celebrate the music and the community surrounding it. The members of BLURRYFACE are massive Twenty One Pilots fans themselves, with a deep understanding of the connection this music creates for people. The band is not trying to imitate or pretend to be Twenty One Pilots. Instead, they aim to honor the experience that Tyler and Josh created by bringing fans together in a safe, welcoming environment where they can express themselves freely, celebrate the music they love, and share in the emotional connection that has always been at the heart of the Twenty One Pilots community. Check out BLURRYFACE here! Website | Instagram ————————————————– *Ticket Alert* Tickets for Mickey’s Black Box are sold through TicketMaster, via our website, or in person at our Box Office. discovery-af5122a256cfed9c20b5911e28bfa2.description: Friday January 22nd, 2027 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | ADVANCE – $37.25 + Fees / DAY OF SHOW – $40.30 + Fees Reserved Riser Seating | ADVANCE – $60.60 + Fees / DAY OF SHOW – $60.60 + Fees Reserved Balcony & Mezzanine Seating | ADVANCE – $60.60 + Fees / DAY OF SHOW – $60.60 + Fees This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Big Fan Presents ————————————————— Introducing SUPER 70’S ROCK SHOW featuring Super Trans AM Get ready for a full-throttle, high-octane trip through the Seventies. It’s an electrifying, immersive concert experience packed with arena anthems and chart-topping radio hits that defined a generation. The 70’s are BACK. Combining unparalleled musicianship with artistic and inspired A/V production, you’ll enjoy revisiting classic singalongs from one of the most definable decades in American history. Performing masterworks from icons such as The Eagles, Hall & Oates, Queen, The Doobie Brothers, Paul McCartney & Wings, Peter Frampton, Foreigner, Kiss, Boston and Journey as well as “Yacht Rock” favorites such as “Still the One” by Orleans and Pilot’s “Magic”, your audience will fall in love with this epic decade of memorable music all over again. In addition to every member of the band taking the lead vocal mic throughout the evening, each show is accompanied by state of the art stage production that pays homage to the era’s unique pop culture. It’s time to dust off your flared jeans, break out the air guitar and take a trip back to the days when Welcome Back Kotter and Happy Days kept us glued to our televisions, Gerald Ford and Jimmy Carter led our nation, kids jumped Evil Kneivel toys over their Matchbox cars and these timeless songs became the soundtrack to our lives. Ladies and gentlemen…Start your engines…Roll down your windows, crank up the radio, and take a ride with the Super 70’s Rock Show Super Trans AM. Check out Super Trans AM here! discovery-440e156e6300a28933c70c088038e2.description: For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440. She’s Got Soul Thursday, April 15, 2027 @ 7:00 PM At the Lancaster County Convention Center 25 S Queen Street, Lancaster, PA 17603 Concert Timing (approx.): 2 Hours (including a 20-minute intermission) Tickets: $50-$120 Powerhouse vocalist Capathia Jenkins brings her stunning presence and electrifying voice to the Lancaster County Convention Center for She's Got Soul, a celebration of R&B and soul music's greatest leading ladies. Fresh from her acclaimed Aretha: A Tribute, Jenkins performs iconic hits from Whitney Houston, Gladys Knight, Chaka Khan, Adele, and many others, backed by a trio of professional singers and the full Lancaster Symphony Orchestra. This show has captivated audiences across the USA and Canada with orchestras including The Cleveland Orchestra, the Utah Symphony, and the Baltimore Symphony. Don't miss this opportunity to experience the timeless power of soul music performed with symphonic brilliance. FEATURING: Ben McNaboe, guest conductor Capathia Jenkins, vocals For questions, assistance, or to purchase tickets over the phone, please call our box office at (717) 291-6440.

discovery-46adf2dc0c9d1d5d1606ba7471b793.title: Monthly Club Meeting – “Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies”
discovery-46adf2dc0c9d1d5d1606ba7471b793.description: Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Club President Andy McGann Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.

discovery-38184a670c16c1eabd74564ef10bfa.title: Crazy Little Thing Called Love at Prima
discovery-38184a670c16c1eabd74564ef10bfa.description: Rock classics. Real heart. Big Laughs. Classic pop-rock favorites burst to life, woven with intimate, cabaret-style moments where performers share funny, heartfelt stories about love — the kind that will have you laughing one minute and leaning a little closer to the person beside you the next. A powerhouse band fuels iconic anthems with electric sing-along energy, while those in-between moments make it feel personal and quite playful. It’s fresh and yet nostalgic — a celebration of love in all its forms and phases — steady, surprising, hard-earned, and deeply felt… in a concert experience that’ll leave you glowing. discovery-eaa31ea99cb8c604ab6c83e205e565.title: Grave Concern: Historic Cemetery Preservation in Lancaster County
discovery-eaa31ea99cb8c604ab6c83e205e565.description: Discover the hidden history right beneath our feet! Join Sam Mecum and Kenn Lefever from Grave Concern, Inc. for an engaging look at the historic burial grounds of Lancaster County and Manheim Township. From forgotten family plots to recent preservation efforts at the Meister cemetery near the Lancaster Airport, learn how local historians protect these vital pieces of our community's heritage-- and what happens when modern development meets historic sites. Registration is encouraged!

discovery-323a1f4cfaef9d0cb2a10287cc2881.title: Southern Lancaster Christmas Bird Count (SoLanCo CBC)
discovery-323a1f4cfaef9d0cb2a10287cc2881.description: All birders are welcome and newcomers will be paired with experienced CBC volunteers. Derek Stoner is the coordinator for the SoLanCo CBC. Contact Derek at (484) 723-3348 or derekstoner@hotmail.com to volunteer and receive instructions and assignments. All birders are welcome and newcomers will be pared with experienced CBC volunteers. Birders are also welcome to do a feeder watch count for the CBC, but you must contact Derek to make sure your property is within the SoLanCo count circle and to receive instructions. IMPORTANT NOTE: If CBCing on State Game Lands, participants must wear blaze orange per new Pennsylvania Game Commission regulations requiring wear on Game Lands Oct. 1 through Jan. 31. Even if not birding Game Lands, wear of blaze orange is strongly encouraged by anyone recreating in any areas open to hunting during this timeframe.

discovery-640c46f37161ace7b26ee4ad5615c0.title: Middle Creek Winter Bird Walk
discovery-640c46f37161ace7b26ee4ad5615c0.description: This field trip offers a hands-on birding experience that will allow participants to explore Middle Creek’s winter landscape and observe the season’s local bird species while gaining insight into the process of counting birds for the Christmas Bird Count (CBC). Whether you’re a seasoned birder or new to birding and CBCs, this outing offers a unique opportunity to connect with nature and learn how birding data is collected in the field each year for this citizen-science survey. Pre-registration is required by 5 p.m the day prior for this offering. Contact Ted at tanicholsii@gmail.com or 717-856-3851 if you have questions or want to make a reservation to attend. IMPORTANT NOTE: Attendees must wear blaze orange for this field trip per new Pennsylvania Game Commission regulations requiring wear on Game Lands Oct. 1 through Jan. 31. Location: Middle Creek Wildlife Management Area Visitor Center, 100 Museum Road, Stevens, PA 17578 Contact: Ted Nichols, 717-856-3851 or tanicholsii@gmail.com.
